items.title: Social network with AI agents – why bad, why good?
items.raw_excerpt:
Hello! I can't get my mind off the idea of building an AI-native social network. Every user has its own agent (only one), which can talk to other agents or check content on the user's behalf.
That way, the agent can "process" far more information about people than the human, and help in building relations. Why it is a bad/good idea? Worth trying?

items.title: Emu Concept – Make AI Follows Your Rules. (Feedback Wanted)
items.raw_excerpt: The idea is how can we make personal agent apps on the phone just listen to your rules... Like it's weird to have Muse, Grok Bot, Dots, Instinct not ask me about when I want them to work for me or align with my rules, values, and goals. If I give these agents access to tools/connectors/data they just "assume" what I want or what it should do rather than asking me? And even if I set these for a specific agent then what happens when a newer personal agent comes out? Do I have to reconfigure again my rules for each flavor of personal agents or harness? This is where our initial idea stems from and we need feedback: Emu is a self-learning on-device AI guardian that makes AI agents follow your rules. Also the video above kind of just highlights Emu's concept thought process.
